title: Closing a Project in Context

header.html: 4.7.1 apply closing a project: activities, inputs and outputs, roles and responsibilities, how the practices are applied; 4.7.2 analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, considering tailoring, the practices, and the purpose and objectives of the process
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

html:
1Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

Closing a project is the process that ends the project in an orderly way. It is the final stage of a planned project, or it is used early when the board stops the project. The figure shows the main flow.

Purpose: provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed, and recognize that the objectives in the PID have been achieved, or that the project has nothing more to contribute.

Objectives: acceptance is verified; products are handed to the people who will operate and support them; performance is reviewed against the baselines; benefits achieved so far are assessed and later benefit reviews are planned; follow-on actions are provided for; lessons are recorded.

Principle How it shows up here
Continued business justification Results are compared with the business case and benefits are followed up
Learn from experience The lessons report goes to the corporate or programme level
Focus on products Acceptance is checked against the acceptance criteria
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships Ownership passes to operations and named owners
Manage by exception A premature close follows a board decision
Exam tip

. Acceptance first, then closure. The project manager recommends closure; the project board authorizes it.

2Activities, inputs and outputs

The names below give the general idea; check the Official Book's wording for the activities.

Activity What the project manager does
Prepare planned closure Checks that all work is done and approved against the project product description; closes or passes on open issues and risks
Prepare premature closure After the board decides to stop early, records what was done and not done, and salvages the products
Hand over products Passes products to those who will operate them; confirms acceptance and that support is in place
Evaluate the project Reviews performance against the PID baselines; writes the end project report and lessons report; plans benefit reviews
Recommend project closure Sends the board the closure recommendation; prepares to release resources and archive records
Flow Main items
Inputs Project product description and acceptance criteria; product approvals; PID baselines; project log; benefits management approach; the board's instruction for a premature close
Outputs End project report; lessons report; follow-on action recommendations; benefits review plan; acceptance and handover records; closure recommendation; archived records

Follow-on actions and the benefits review plan travel with the end project report and the benefits management approach. Check the book for where each is held.

Exam tip

. Benefits are reviewed after the project, so closing needs a benefits review plan with an owner. Keeping a project open to measure benefits is a red flag.

3Roles

Role Area of focus in this process
Project manager Responsible: plans and carries out closure, hands over, writes the reports, recommends closure
Project board Receives the recommendation and authorizes closure, in directing a project
Executive Confirms the objectives were met; makes sure benefit reviews have an owner
Senior user Confirms the products meet user needs and are accepted for use
Senior supplier Confirms supplier work is complete and supports the handover
Team manager Hands over delivered products and their records
Project assurance Checks independently that acceptance is real and the reports are fair
Project support Archives records, closes the logs, helps prepare the reports

Check the book's roles table. Lessons and follow-on actions go to the corporate or programme level, which also tracks benefits.

4How the practices are applied

Practice How it is applied in closing a project
Business case Compare results with the business case; plan benefit reviews
Organization Hand over to operations; release the team and suppliers
Plans Compare actuals with the baselined plans
Quality Confirm every product meets its acceptance criteria
Risk Pass residual risks on to named owners
Issues Close open issues or pass them on as follow-on actions
Progress End project report, lessons report, and final update of the logs

5Judging a scenario

Effective approach Red flag: not fit for purpose
Acceptance confirmed against the criteria by the right people Closure recommended before acceptance, or acceptance assumed
Products handed to operations with training and support Operations left unready, so the service fails
End project report compares results with the PID baselines A report that only lists activities
Benefits reviewed after the project, with an owner, dates and measures Benefit tracking ends when the team disbands
Follow-on actions, open issues and risks passed to named owners Unfinished work disappears or is called phase two with no record
Lessons sent to the corporate or programme level Lessons stay in the project manager's head
Premature close: the board decides, the project manager salvages, hands over and records The project is abandoned, or the project manager stops it alone

Tailoring changes the size of the closure, not the confirmation of acceptance:

  • Small projects: a short end project report, lessons in the log and one acceptance and handover meeting.
  • Agile or incremental delivery: earlier releases are already accepted; closing confirms the final state, and unfinished backlog items become follow-on actions.
  • Supplier projects: confirm each contract is complete under the commercial management approach, and release suppliers.
  • Sustainability, digital and data: retire the old process safely, archive or dispose of data by the rules, and add sustainability measures to the benefit reviews.
Exam tip

. A premature close still uses closing a project: salvage, hand over, record, learn. The board decides to stop, and the project manager does not simply walk away.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1At the end of Project Harbor's rollout stage, Sam Okafor sends the board an end project report and recommends closure. Tomas Reyes, the senior user, has not yet confirmed that the permit service meets the acceptance criteria. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because the project manager decides when the project closes
  • BNo, because acceptance must come before a recommendation to close
  • CYes, because acceptance can be confirmed after the project has closed
  • DNo, because the end project report must be written by the executive
Show the answer

Answer: B. Closing a project is the fixed point at which acceptance is confirmed, so it comes before the recommendation, and the board then authorizes closure.

S2Project Harbor's permit service is live and accepted. The port's operations team has had no training and has no support guide. What should Sam do before recommending closure?

  • ARecommend closure now and leave support to operations
  • BKeep the project open until all the benefits are realized
  • CArrange a handover with training and support information
  • DAsk Delta Software to run the service on its own indefinitely
Show the answer

Answer: C. Handing products over so that operations can support them is part of closing a project, and benefits are reviewed after the project.

S3The port's board cancels Project Harbor after the build stage because permits will be outsourced. Sam salvages the finished products, hands them to the port's IT team, records what was not done and why, writes the lessons and recommends closure. Was this an appropriate action, and why?

  • AYes, because a premature close still hands over and records lessons
  • BYes, because a cancelled project needs no end project report or lessons
  • CNo, because the closing a project process is only for finished projects
  • DNo, because an early close should not involve the project board at all
Show the answer

Answer: A. A premature close uses closing a project to salvage value, hand over, record and learn, with the board's authority.

S4Project Harbor's permit service is complete. Who should confirm that it meets the users' needs and acceptance criteria?

  • ALena Kovac, the senior supplier
  • BWei Chen, the team manager
  • CAisha Bello, the assurance lead
  • DTomas Reyes, the senior user
Show the answer

Answer: D. The senior user speaks for the users and confirms that the products meet their needs, while project assurance only checks independently.

S5Sam must give the board a review of how Project Harbor performed against the budget, time, quality and benefits baselined in the PID. Which management product provides this?

  • AEnd stage report
  • BEnd project report
  • CHighlight report
  • DBenefits review plan
Show the answer

Answer: B. The end project report reviews the whole project against its baselines at closure.

S6Sam proposes to close Project Harbor once the service is accepted and handed over, with a benefits review six months later and a named owner. Was this an appropriate approach, and why?

  • ANo, because the project cannot close until every benefit is fully measured
  • BNo, because benefit reviews are the project manager's job after closure
  • CYes, because benefits appear after the project, so an owner reviews them
  • DYes, because benefits do not need to be reviewed after the project ends
Show the answer

Answer: C. Many benefits only appear after the project, so a benefits review plan with an owner continues the follow-up.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of closing a project?

Show the answer

To provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the PID objectives are recognized as achieved.

R2Name the five activities.

Show the answer

Prepare planned closure, prepare premature closure, hand over products, evaluate the project and recommend project closure.

R3Which two reports does the project manager write to evaluate the project?

Show the answer

The end project report and the lessons report.

R4Who authorizes project closure?

Show the answer

The project board, on the project manager's recommendation.

R5What is a premature close?

Show the answer

Closing the project early because the board decides to stop it.

R6Why are benefits reviewed after the project?

Show the answer

Many benefits only appear after the project has ended.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose confirm acceptance and that the PID objectives are achieved
Activities planned closure, premature closure, hand over, evaluate, recommend closure
Outputs end project report, lessons report, follow-on actions, benefits review plan
Decision the project manager recommends; the board authorizes
Effective acceptance, handover, honest report, benefit reviews with an owner
Red flags no acceptance, unready operations, benefits dropped, abandoned project
Premature close board stops; salvage, hand over, record, learn
Tailoring smaller closure, never skipping acceptance
